data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: eager
sections.summary: Very keen and wanting very much to do or have something.

senses.definition: very keen and wanting very much to do or have something; showing a lot of enthusiasm and interest
examples: He was eager to learn everything about his new role.

answers.answer: She was eager to start her new job.
She was eager about to start.

sections.question: embarrassed
sections.summary: Feeling ashamed or self-conscious because of something awkward.

senses.definition: feeling ashamed or self-conscious because of something awkward you have done or that has happened to you
examples: She felt embarrassed when she tripped in front of everyone.

answers.answer: He felt embarrassed after forgetting her name.

sections.question: enthusiastic
sections.summary: Feeling or showing great excitement and interest in something.

senses.definition: feeling or showing great excitement and interest in something; having a lot of enthusiasm
examples: He was enthusiastic about the new challenge at work.

answers.answer: She was enthusiastic about the project.

sections.question: envious
sections.summary: Wishing you had something that another person has; feeling envy.

senses.definition: wishing you had something that another person has; feeling unhappy because someone else has something you want
examples: She was envious of her friend's new laptop.

answers.answer: He was envious of his brother's success.

sections.question: excited
sections.summary: Feeling very happy and enthusiastic, especially about something that is going to happen.

senses.definition: feeling very happy and enthusiastic, especially about something that is going to happen
examples: The children were excited about the school trip.

answers.answer: She was excited about the trip.

sections.question: grateful
sections.summary: Feeling or showing thanks because someone has helped you or been kind.

senses.definition: feeling or showing that you want to thank someone because they have helped you or done something kind for you
examples: We are grateful for all the support you have given us.

answers.answer: I am grateful for your support.
I am grateful to your support.

sections.question: humiliated
sections.summary: Made to feel deeply ashamed and embarrassed, especially in front of others.

senses.definition: made to feel very ashamed and embarrassed, especially in front of other people
examples: He felt humiliated when his answer was wrong in front of the whole class.

answers.answer: He felt humiliated after the public criticism.

sections.question: inquisitive
sections.summary: Curious and eager to learn or find out new things.

senses.definition: interested in learning about many different things; curious and eager to find out information
examples: An inquisitive mind is a great advantage when studying science.

answers.answer: The child was inquisitive and asked many questions.
The child inquisitive about the answer.

sections.question: interested
sections.summary: Giving attention to something because you want to know more about it or enjoy it.

senses.definition: giving attention to something because you want to know more about it or you enjoy it
examples: He was interested in the history of the local town.

answers.answer: She is interested in learning Spanish.

sections.question: jealous
sections.summary: Feeling unhappy and angry because someone else has something you want.

senses.definition: feeling unhappy and angry because someone else has something you want, or because someone you care about is paying attention to another person
examples: She felt jealous when her colleague got the promotion.

answers.answer: He was jealous of his friend's promotion.
